risks.note: The Board attributes the adverse move in Operating Profit Margin, Net Profit Margin, Return on Equity and ROCE mainly to 'Lower Profit from PDD due to loss of institutional / tender business particularly from USAID and UNFPA'. A division whose profitability turns on a small number of aid-agency and government tender relationships is structurally exposed to donor-funding and procurement decisions outside the Company's control.
risks.risk: Institutional / tender business concentration in the Protective Devices Division

risks.note: The same explanatory note flags 'reduced margins on new businesses' alongside the tender loss - volume replaced at a lower margin, so a recovery in revenue does not automatically restore the earlier profit pool.
risks.risk: Margin dilution on the replacement business won after the tender losses

risks.note: 'Higher Brand promotional expenses relating to CPD and Pleasure products' is cited as a driver of the adverse margin and return ratios - a structural cost of competing in FMCG and the sexual-wellness category, where spend must be sustained to hold shelf and share.
risks.risk: Rising brand-promotion intensity in Consumer Products and Pleasure Products

risks.note: Return on Investment was negative in both years and worsened - 'Return on Investment is negative due to reduction in the market value of Equity Investments'. A material investment book means reported returns move with the market, independent of operating performance.
risks.risk: Mark-to-market exposure on the equity investment portfolio

risks.note: The Board notes 'Higher Exceptional Income (Net) in the previous year vis-a-vis the current year' as a reason ratios look adverse; with exceptional items appearing in successive years, headline profit trends require adjustment before they can be read as operating trends.
risks.risk: Earnings comparability distorted by recurring exceptional items

risks.note: The BRSR reports 5 total recordable work-related injuries among Workers in 2025-26 (22 in 2024-25) and one worker fatality in 2024-25, against nil for Employees in both years. Every recorded injury and the fatality sit in the Workers category - the shop-floor population - even though LTIFR is reported as nil.

Only 15.53% of male workers and no female workers received a performance and career development review in 2025-26, while employee reviews reached 86.02% - a retention and development gap on the shop floor. (The permanent-employee turnover trend table sits in the BRSR Section A block, which was routed to other domains in this bundle set, not here.)

'Implementation of Oracle Discreet Manufacturing module at Ortho Division is in progress' in the division growing fastest, where SKU counts are rising; IT resilience rests on empanelled vendors and Commvault endpoint backups. A disrupted cutover would hit the division carrying the growth expectations.
risks.risk: Execution risk in the ERP / IT transition
